svg.title: Cite text evidence
svg.desc: A short passage in a box with one sentence highlighted: "each night the water crept a little higher up the bank." An arrow leads to a speech bubble that reads "I think Amara is worried about a flood, because the text says 'each night the water crept a little higher.'" A second bubble reads "I think she is preparing, because the text says 'the village must move the rice sacks to higher ground.'" Labels and shapes, not color alone, carry the meaning so the graphic prints clearly in grayscale.
svg.text: Amara watched the river rise each evening after the rains. She
counted the logs that floated past — three, then five, then twelve —
and each night the water crept a little higher up the bank.
When the water reached the roots of the old baobab tree, Amara knew
the village must move the rice sacks to higher ground.
"I think Amara is worried about a flood, because the text says
'each night the water crept a little higher.'"
idea → evidence, joined by "because the text says"
"I think she is preparing, because the text says
'the village must move the rice sacks to higher ground.'"
the words hold up the idea
An interpretation without evidence is a guess.
